alternatives.argument: Complete local proof: choose 0<r0<R0<a and a smooth spatial bump f equal to one on B_r0 and supported in B_R0, so F=integral f>0. Choose compactly supported smooth G,H equal respectively to (t-u)^2 and (t-u)^3 on a neighborhood of [u-a/c,u+a/c]. Set rho=-G partial_3 f and J=G′ f e3+H′(-partial_3 f e1+partial_1 f e3). Smoothness and compact support follow from the bump and time cutoffs. The continuity equation follows from rho_t=-G′ partial_3 f and div J=G′ partial_3 f+H′(-partial_1 partial_3 f+partial_3 partial_1 f)=G′ partial_3 f. Integration by parts on a ball containing supp f gives integral partial_i f=0; the controlled dipole identity therefore gives p″(u)=integral J_t(y,u)dy=G″(u)F e3=2F e3, so the dipole transverse amplitude at n=e3 is zero. The exact shifted-current component is V_1(e3,u)=-integral H″(u+y3/c) partial_3 f(y)dy=(1/c)integral f(y)H‴(u+y3/c)dy=6F/c>0, again by compact-support integration by parts and the chosen cubic interval. The transverse-radiation theorem then gives E_rad(e3,u)=mu0/(4pi)e3 cross (e3 cross V(e3,u)) nonzero. Thus the relative error with the dipole amplitude as denominator is undefined at this node, despite the absolute error estimate.
